verses.1:1: Simeon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have received a faith of equal worth with ours by the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
verses.1:2: May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the full knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: Seeing that His divine power has granted to us all things pertaining to life and godliness, through the full knowledge of the One who called us by His own glory and virtue,
verses.1:4: through which He has granted to us the precious and very great promises, so that through these you may become sharers in the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through desire.
verses.1:5: Now for this very reason also, applying all diligence, supply virtue in your faith, and in your virtue, knowledge,
verses.1:6: and in your knowledge, self-control, and in your self-control, endurance, and in your endurance, godliness,
verses.1:7: and in your godliness, brotherly affection, and in your brotherly affection, love.
verses.1:8: For if these qualities belong to you and increase, they render you neither idle nor unfruitful toward the full knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: For the one who lacks these things is blind, being shortsighted, having forgotten the cleansing of his former sins.
verses.1:10: Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election firm; for by doing these things you will never stumble.
verses.1:11: For in this way the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
verses.1:12: Therefore I intend always to remind you about these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth present with you.
verses.1:13: And I consider it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by way of reminder,
verses.1:14: knowing that the laying aside of my tent is imminent, just as our Lord Jesus Christ also made clear to me.
verses.1:15: And I will also be diligent so that at every time after my departure you may be able to call these things to remembrance.
verses.1:16: For we did not follow skillfully crafted myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; rather, we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.
verses.1:17: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when such a voice was brought to Him by the Majestic Glory: "This is My Son, My beloved, with whom I am well pleased."
verses.1:18: And we ourselves heard this voice brought from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
verses.1:19: And we have the prophetic word made more certain, to which you do well to pay attention as to a lamp shining in a murky place, until day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts;
verses.1:20: knowing this first of all, that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one's own interpretation;
verses.1:21: for no prophecy was ever brought by human will, but men spoke from God as they were borne along by the Holy Spirit.
verses.2:1: Yet false prophets also arose among the people, just as false teachers will be among you as well, who will covertly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who purchased them, bringing swift ruin upon themselves.
verses.2:2: And many will follow their sensual ways, and because of them the way of truth will be reviled.
verses.2:3: And in greed they will exploit you with fabricated words; their judgment from long ago is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.
verses.2:4: For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and handed them over to pits of gloomy darkness to be kept for judgment;
verses.2:5: and did not spare the ancient world, but protected Noah, a herald of righteousness, along with seven others, when He brought a flood upon the world of ungodly people;
verses.2:6: and by reducing the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes condemned them to ruin, having set them as an example for those who are going to live ungodly lives;
verses.2:7: and rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the sensual conduct of lawless people—
verses.2:8: for by sight and hearing, that righteous man, while dwelling among them day after day, tormented his righteous soul over their lawless deeds—
verses.2:9: then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,
verses.2:10: and especially those who walk after the flesh in the desire of defilement and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they do not tremble as they revile glorious ones,
verses.2:11: whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a reviling judgment against them before the Lord.
verses.2:12: But these people, like unreasoning animals, born by nature for capture and destruction, reviling things of which they are ignorant, will also be destroyed in their own destruction,
verses.2:13: suffering wrong as the wages of wrongdoing. They consider it pleasure to revel in the daytime; they are stains and blemishes, reveling in their deceptions while feasting with you,
verses.2:14: having eyes full of adultery and never ceasing from sin, enticing unstable souls, having a heart trained in greed—children of a curse.
verses.2:15: Abandoning the straight way, they have gone astray, having followed the way of Balaam, son of Bosor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing,
verses.2:16: but he received a rebuke for his own transgression: a speechless donkey, speaking with a human voice, restrained the madness of the prophet.
verses.2:17: These people are waterless springs and mists driven by a storm, for whom the gloom of darkness has been reserved.
verses.2:18: For speaking arrogant words of emptiness, they entice through the desires of the flesh, by sensual ways, those who are barely escaping from the ones who live in error,
verses.2:19: promising them freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whatever a person is overcome, to this he has been enslaved.
verses.2:20: For if, after having escaped the defilements of the world through the full knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in these things and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first.
verses.2:21: For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment handed down to them.
verses.2:22: What the true proverb says has happened to them: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and, "A washed sow to wallowing in the mire."
verses.3:1: Beloved, this is already the second letter I am writing to you, in both of which I am awakening your sincere mind through a reminder,
verses.3:2: that you should remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets and the commandment of the Lord and Savior given through your apostles,
verses.3:3: knowing this first of all, that in the last days mockers will come with mocking, walking according to their own desires
verses.3:4: and saying, "Where is the promise of His coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things remain just as they were from the beginning of creation."
verses.3:5: For they deliberately overlook this fact, that heavens existed from long ago, and an earth formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
verses.3:6: through which the world of that time, being flooded with water, perished.
verses.3:7: But by the same word the present heavens and earth have been stored up for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly people.
verses.3:8: But do not let this one thing escape your notice, beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
verses.3:9: The Lord does not delay regarding the promise, as some regard delay, but is patient toward you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
verses.3:10: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will be dissolved with intense heat, and the earth and the works in it will be found.
verses.3:11: Since all these things are thus to be dissolved, what sort of people ought you to be in holy conduct and acts of godliness,
verses.3:12: awaiting and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be set on fire and dissolved, and the elements will melt with intense heat!
verses.3:13: But according to His promise we are awaiting new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
verses.3:14: Therefore, beloved, since you are awaiting these things, be diligent to be found by Him spotless and blameless, in peace.
verses.3:15: And regard the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
verses.3:16: as he also does in all his letters when speaking in them about these things. In them there are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unstable distort, as they also do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
verses.3:17: You therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, be on your guard so that you are not carried away by the error of lawless people and fall from your own stability;
verses.3:18: but grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

notes.1:1: Greek "tou theou hemon kai soteros Iesou Christou" places a single article before both nouns, identifying Jesus Christ as both "our God and Savior," though a few interpreters take it as referring to God and the Savior Jesus Christ separately.
notes.1:19: Greek "bebaioteron" can be read predicatively ("made more certain" or confirmed by the Transfiguration) or attributively ("we have an even more reliable prophetic word").
notes.1:20: Greek "idias epilyseos" ("one's own interpretation") is debated: in light of v. 21, many take it to mean a prophet's own origination or explanation of a revelation, while others understand it as an individual's private interpretation.
notes.2:4: The verb "tartarosas" ("cast into Tartarus") occurs only here in the New Testament, referring to the deepest realm of punishment. The Greek text reads "seirois" ("pits" or "caverns"), whereas many later manuscripts read "seirais" ("chains").
notes.2:10: Greek "doxas" (literally "glories") refers to exalted spiritual beings or angelic authorities, as reflected in the contrast with angels in v. 11.
notes.2:13: The Greek text reads "adikoumenoi" ("suffering wrong" or "harm"), forming a wordplay with "adikias" ("wrongdoing"), while some manuscripts read "komioumenoi" ("receiving"). It also reads "apatais" ("deceptions") rather than the variant "agapais" ("love feasts").
notes.2:15: Greek "Bosor" corresponds to Hebrew "Beor," the father of Balaam in Numbers 22:5.
notes.3:10: The Greek text reads "heurethesetai" ("will be found," often understood as "exposed" or "laid bare" for judgment), whereas other manuscripts read "katakaesetai" ("will be burned up") or "ouch heurethesetai" ("will not be found"). Greek "stoicheia" ("elements") may refer either to the basic physical components of the cosmos or to heavenly bodies.
notes.3:12: Greek "speudontas" can mean either "hastening" (speeding the arrival of God's day through faithful living) or "earnestly desiring."
notes.3:16: Greek "en hais" ("in them") is feminine plural and refers to Paul's letters ("epistolais"), though some manuscripts read neuter "en hois" ("in these matters").
